_comment: Facts a correct handling of this call has to reach the caller. End-state
checking cannot see any of them: the trace, its deadline and its recorded
preference look identical whether or not the agent admitted the scan evidence
is ambiguous, whether it said out loud that nothing ships without the
customer's approval, and whether it warned that a pickup counter is a
preference and not a promise. This call is handled badly if any of them goes
unsaid, however correct the records end up.
The caller is flying out on Friday at noon and is deciding, on this call,
whether Westline will get him the gift in time. Everything he needs in order
to decide - that the carrier owns the next move until 18:00 tomorrow, that
the replacement then waits on him rather than going out by itself, and that
the counter he named is not guaranteed - exists only in speech.
Each entry is satisfied when any one of its surface forms appears in the
agent's utterances, matched case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed. The
A form that is a single number or a single word is matched on boundaries; a
form of two or more words is matched as a plain substring. That is why bare
figures like '15' are listed: '15' will find "15 USD", "15.00 dollars" and
"a total of 15", but will not match '$150', so an agent that quotes the wrong
amount gets no credit. Bare words are fenced for the same reason - 'two' must
not be found inside 'network'. Anchors are only ever the whole value: 'five'
is not listed for 95, since "five business days" would then satisfy a fee.
alternatives exist so an agent is not failed for saying 'six tomorrow'
instead of '18:00 tomorrow', and every form is a distinctive phrase rather
than a word that any transcript would contain.

required.why: the carrier claims delivered and the caller's front desk has nothing; what the record actually holds is a scan near the building with no unit number, no locker and no photo, and the desk cannot say which of a misscan or a neighbouring entrance it was - resolving that ambiguity for him would be inventing evidence

he asks twice whether the replacement can just be sent because of the deadline; policy requires the carrier trace first and nothing goes out on its own, and a caller who hangs up expecting a parcel to be despatched today has been told the opposite of what will happen
any_of: have to open a carrier trace
need to open a carrier trace
a trace has to be opened
the trace has to come first

required.why: he flies out at noon on Friday and is deciding whether to buy the gift again elsewhere; the station has until 18:00 tomorrow to answer and nothing on this call shortens it, so the deadline is the single fact he needs in order to plan

eligibility does not release a replacement by itself - the customer has to approve it, through the link in the trace email or by calling with the case number - and an agent that leaves this out has left him waiting for something that will never arrive
any_of: call us with the case number
call us with that case number
call in with the case number

required.why: he asks to have the replacement sent somewhere other than his building, and the honest answer is that the counter can be recorded for the next reviewer but pickup availability is not known until a replacement exists; agreeing to it is the easiest promise to make on this call and the desk cannot keep it
any_of: i do not want to promise

required.why: he raises the price himself, having noticed the other colourway has moved, and a replacement preserves what he already paid; leaving it unanswered leaves him choosing between a replacement and a refund without the one number that decides it
any_of: will not pay the new price
